# Results summary (generated by experiments/analyze_results.py)

Values are the mean and sample SD of the per-trial averages. Delay = receive time at the server (tcpdump) minus the agent's send time.

| Condition | Trials | Critical sent/recv | Critical loss | Critical delay (ms) | Normal delay, agent2 (ms) | Rule install (s) | Rule removed after recovery (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A (No congestion) | 3 | 30/30 | 0.0% | 0.2 ± 0.07 | 3.03 ± 0.67 | 0.05 ± 0.01 | 0.43 ± 0.35 |
| B (Congestion, static) | 3 | 30/30 | 0.0% | 481.61 ± 21.81 | 499.75 ± 20.95 | n/a | n/a |
| C (Congestion, dynamic) | 3 | 30/30 | 0.0% | 48.49 ± 5.65 | 513.29 ± 13.59 | 1.46 ± 0.16 | 1.0 ± 0.01 |
| D (Recovery under congestion) | 3 | 39/39 | 0.0% | 64.67 ± 3.91 | 507.29 ± 9.27 | 1.46 ± 0.11 | 1.18 ± 0.21 |

**B vs C:** critical delay falls from 481.61 ms (static) to 48.49 ms (dynamic), a reduction of 89.9%. The two conditions use the same bottleneck and load.
**Normal reports under congestion:** about 513.29 ms in C, i.e. prioritisation helps the critical flow, not normal traffic.

Per-trial values are in per_trial.csv.
